summary: Sold-Out feature tested end-to-end. Backend pytest: 13/13 pass in /app/backend/tests/test_sold_out.py — vendor toggle endpoint (auth/RBAC + happy path + 404), /api/drops hides sold-out surplus (Veg Momos disappears), /api/restaurants/{vendor_id} excludes sold-out items from BOTH surplus_items and menu_items lists, POST /api/orders/create returns HTTP 400 with detail 'This item is sold out' for BOTH surplus (Veg Momos) and takeaway (Paneer Roll) — verified this 400 is raised BEFORE the razorpay_client check (server.py L690-703 executes before L717), and toggling back to in_stock=True fully restores visibility + orderability. Frontend (mobile 390x844, vendor soldouttest@test.com/vendor123): Dashboard > Menu shows Sold Out switch per item with testID toggle-soldout-menu_81837cef4ee5 and toggle-soldout-menu_38278f385303. Toggling ON greys the card, shows 'SOLD OUT' badge and red caption 'Sold out — hidden from customers (auto-resets at midnight)'. Toggling OFF restores 'Available to customers'. Both test items left at in_stock=True.
critical_code_review_comments: Nit: /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/dashboard.tsx L270 uses `onValueChange={() => toggleStock(item.menu_item_id, soldOut)}` which ignores the new value emitted by Switch and instead passes the OLD `soldOut` (which equals the desired new in_stock). Behaviour is correct because of the inversion, but it's non-obvious — a more readable form would be `onValueChange={(v) => toggleStock(item.menu_item_id, !v)}` where `v` is the new sold-out state. Not a bug.

Nit: /app/backend/server.py `toggle_menu_stock` (L1510) sets `sold_out_at = today_ist_str()` on every False-toggle even if the item was already sold out earlier the same day. That effectively resets the stamp to today and is compatible with the midnight-reset design, but if the intent was to preserve the FIRST sold-out timestamp, add `sold_out_at: {$exists: false}` guard. Current behaviour looks intentional.
